cloze.title: 四选一完形填空
cloze.instruction: 阅读节选，为每一空选择最符合原文语境的选项，每题只有一个正确答案。

parts.text: MMX launched successfully on October 19 atop an H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan. About two weeks ago,

controllers received the first signal from the spacecraft to check it is communicating normally.

Studying small bodies and comparing them with meteorites – natural samples of space rocks that reach Earth – helps scientists understand the

and evolution of the Solar System.

Observations from the Soviet Union’s Phobos 2 spacecraft, which gathered data from its position in Martian orbit in 1989, and by researchers using Nasa’s Infrared Telescope Facility in the 2010s, have provided important

about Phobos’ origins.

They showed that the Martian moon has spectral properties (the way a planetary surface absorbs and reflects light, providing information about its composition) resembling those of dark,

asteroids known as D-types. These are thought to have originated in the outer Solar System before some migrated towards the Sun.

For Mars to have captured two separate asteroids would be difficult to explain. An alternative

suggests that Mars captured fragments of an asteroid torn apart by its gravity. These fragments subsequently formed a disc of material from which the moons evolved.

However, this raises the question of how an object from the

outer Solar System reached Mars. Another theory proposes that Phobos and Deimos formed from debris ejected into orbit when a large object struck Mars.

Although this scenario can explain aspects of their orbits, questions remain about whether their composition

that expected from such an impact. Distinguishing between these possibilities is a major goal of the MMX mission, which will investigate both moons and return samples from Phobos to Earth.

What if Phobos contains material from

? Mars’ largest moon may hold another important clue: material delivered from another part of the Solar System.

Large impacts on Mars can eject rocks into space, some of which could eventually land on Phobos. Asteroids striking the moon directly could also leave fragments behind. Scientists call this

material.

Preparing for MMX

About ten years ago, I investigated this process through laboratory experiments and numerical simulations. My research demonstrated that objects
with another planetary body can leave material on a target’s surface even at relatively low-impact velocities.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

options: Scientists are developing ways to select valuable soil samples from the Martian moon Phobos.
Crystals inside volcanoes can preserve signals that help researchers understand approaching eruptions.
Safety practices in hazardous industries offer lessons for regulating artificial intelligence.
Whether AI agents have minds depends on difficult philosophical questions about thought and agency.
